_comment: One entry per published article. Read by the pitch filter (cooldowns, dup-thesis check) and fed to writers as recent-context. Newest last.

entries.thesis: Dirty Magic, Winterfell Whitewalkers, and SHMEATtheBOY are the three teams worth watching in 2026 — everyone else is noise.
The Howlin' Wolf's three-year prediction streak is verifiable in exactly one of three seasons, and in that one season he named multiple contenders and claimed the streak on whichever happened to win.

Before a single game has been played, Winterfell Whitewalkers and Macon Muskrats made the league's first real trade of the year, and it's the kind of move that tells you what both of them think they're building.
Dirty Magic adding Amon-Ra St. Brown and Kyren Williams is a masterclass in aggressive leadership, and anyone crying about roster balance needs to shut up and play the game.

While the rest of the league scrambles to ship high-profile veterans in August, Josh Cochran is patiently laying down a real, sustainable dynasty foundation that will outlast the current contender push.
Tuesday's piece on JUICE misstated two trade details: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Kyren Williams went to Dirty Magic, not Topeka Cosbies, and Nico Collins went to AthensAssholes, not Dirty Magic.

By surrendering a rookie receiver and an aging tight end for two elite, volume-proven assets, Dirty Magic executed a textbook value-extraction trade that shifts their contention window immediately forward while Topeka Cosbies absorbed significant prospective risk.
Evan Plowden's reluctance to either bottom out or mortgage the future leaves his roster in a perpetual holding pattern that might be entirely intentional.
Macon Muskrats took the trophy last year on the back of my preseason ink and now Griffin Bear walks around this league like he invented the forward pass all by himself.
Contention windows in twelve-team dynasty leagues are routinely overestimated by eighteen months due to the emotional weighting managers assign to brand-name assets.
